question: A toy company makes toys and knows that most of their customers are young boys and girls. To reach these groups, the company has decided to purchase commercial spots on cartoons and kids-movies. Each cartoon is seen by 2 millions young boys and 1 million young girls. Each kids-movie is seen by 4 million young boys and 6 million young girls. The company wants their commercials to be seen by at least 30 million young boys and 40 million young girls. If a commercial during a cartoon costs $5000 and a commercial during a kids-movie costs $12000, how many of each should be purchased to minimize cost?

import pyomo.environ as pyo

DATA = {
    # media: 0 = cartoon, 1 = kids-movie
    "media": [0, 1],
    # audience groups: 0 = young boys, 1 = young girls
    "groups": [0, 1],
    # cost per commercial of each medium (index aligns with media)
    "cost": [5000, 12000],
    # audience reach (millions) matrix: reach[group][medium]
    "reach": [
        [2, 4],  # young boys per cartoon, per kids-movie
        [1, 6],  # young girls per cartoon, per kids-movie
    ],
    # minimum required reach (millions) per audience group
    "min_reach": [30, 40],
}


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA
    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    model.J = pyo.Set(initialize=d["media"], ordered=True)
    model.I = pyo.Set(initialize=d["groups"], ordered=True)

    # x[j] = number of commercials purchased of medium j (nonnegative integers)
    def x_bounds(m, j):
        return (0, None)

    model.x = pyo.Var(model.J, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers, bounds=x_bounds)

    # Objective: minimize total cost of purchased commercials
    def obj_rule(m):
        return sum(d["cost"][j] * m.x[j] for j in m.J)

    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.minimize)

    # Reach constraint per audience group: sum_j reach[i][j]*x[j] >= min_reach[i]
    def reach_rule(m, i):
        return sum(d["reach"][i][j] * m.x[j] for j in m.J) >= d["min_reach"][i]

    model.reach = pyo.Constraint(model.I, rule=reach_rule)

    return model

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Problem: Toy company buys commercials on cartoons and kids-movies.
#
# Decision variables
#   x_cartoon : number of cartoon commercials purchased  (NonNegativeIntegers)
#   x_movie   : number of kids-movie commercials purchased (NonNegativeIntegers)
#
# Objective (minimize)
#   total cost = 5000 * x_cartoon + 12000 * x_movie
#
# Constraints
#   (1) Boys reach:  2 * x_cartoon + 4 * x_movie >= 30   (millions of boys)
#   (2) Girls reach: 1 * x_cartoon + 6 * x_movie >= 40   (millions of girls)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

DATA = {
    "boys_cartoon": 2,      # millions of boys per cartoon commercial
    "boys_movie": 4,        # millions of boys per kids-movie commercial
    "girls_cartoon": 1,     # millions of girls per cartoon commercial
    "girls_movie": 6,       # millions of girls per kids-movie commercial
    "min_boys": 30,         # required millions of boys
    "min_girls": 40,        # required millions of girls
    "cost_cartoon": 5000,   # dollars per cartoon commercial
    "cost_movie": 12000,    # dollars per kids-movie commercial
}


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA
    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    # Decision variables
    model.x_cartoon = pyo.Var(within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers)
    model.x_movie = pyo.Var(within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers)

    # Objective: minimize total cost
    model.obj = pyo.Objective(
        expr=d["cost_cartoon"] * model.x_cartoon
        + d["cost_movie"] * model.x_movie,
        sense=pyo.minimize,
    )

    # Constraint (1): boys reach
    model.boys_reach = pyo.Constraint(
        expr=d["boys_cartoon"] * model.x_cartoon
        + d["boys_movie"] * model.x_movie
        >= d["min_boys"]
    )

    # Constraint (2): girls reach
    model.girls_reach = pyo.Constraint(
        expr=d["girls_cartoon"] * model.x_cartoon
        + d["girls_movie"] * model.x_movie
        >= d["min_girls"]
    )

    return model

"""
Toy Company Advertising Mill MILP

Decision variables (index set P = commercial types):
    x[p] >= 0 integer  –  number of commercials purchased of type p

Objective (minimize):
    total cost = sum_p COST[p] * x[p]

Constraints:
  (1) Source: "commercials seen by at least 30 million young boys"
        -> sum_p BOYS[p] * x[p] >= MIN_BOYS
  (2) Source: "commercials seen by at least 40 million young girls"
        -> sum_p GIRLS[p] * x[p] >= MIN_GIRLS
"""

import pyomo.environ as pyo

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- DATA
DATA = {
    # set / index
    "PLATFORMS": ["cartoon", "kids_movie"],
    # cost in dollars per commercial
    "COST": {
        "cartoon": 5000,
        "kids_movie": 12000,
    },
    # millions of young boys reached per commercial (one play)
    "BOYS": {
        "cartoon": 2,
        "kids_movie": 4,
    },
    # millions of young girls reached per commercial
    "GIRLS": {
        "cartoon": 1,
        "kids_movie": 6,
    },
    # required minimum audience in millions
    "MIN_BOYS": 30,
    "MIN_GIRLS": 40,
}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- BUILD
def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    # --- Sets ---------------------------------------------------------
    model.P = pyo.Set(initialize=d["PLATFORMS"], doc="commercial types")

    # --- Parameters (kept as plain data values accessed below) ---------
    # costs/impart don't need Pyomo Param but keeping names aligned:
    cost = d["COST"]
    boys_reach = d["BOYS"]
    girls_reach = d["GIRLS"]
    min_boys = d["MIN_BOYS"]
    min_girls = d["MIN_GIRLS"]

    # --- Variables ----------------------------------------------------
    # number of commercials of each type, non-negative integers
    model.x = pyo.Var(model.P, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers, doc="commercials bought")

    # --- Objective: minimize total cost -------------------------------
    def obj_rule(m):
        return sum(cost[p] * m.x[p] for p in m.P)

    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.minimize)

    # --- Constraint (1): audience of young boys >= MIN_BOYS ------------
    def boys_rule(m):
        return sum(boys_reach[p] * m.x[p] for p in m.P) >= min_boys

    model.boys = pyo.Constraint(rule=boys_rule, doc="at least MIN_BOYS million young boys reached")

    # --- Constraint (2): audience of young girls >= MIN_GIRLS ---------
    def girls_rule(m):
        return sum(girls_reach[p] * m.x[p] for p in m.P) >= min_girls

    model.girls = pyo.Constraint(rule=girls_rule, doc="at least MIN_GIRLS million young girls reached")

    return model

    "boys_per_cartoon": 2,

def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA
    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    # Sets: media types and audience groups
    model.M = pyo.Set(initialize=["cartoon", "kids_movie"])
    model.G = pyo.Set(initialize=["boys", "girls"])

    # Decision variable: number of commercials of each media type
    model.x = pyo.Var(model.M, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers)

    # Objective: minimise total purchase cost
    def obj_rule(m):
        return (
            d["cost_cartoon"] * m.x["cartoon"]
            + d["cost_kids_movie"] * m.x["kids_movie"]
        )

    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.minimize)

    # Exposure coefficient lookup
    exposure = {
        ("boys", "cartoon"): d["boys_per_cartoon"],
        ("boys", "kids_movie"): d["boys_per_kids_movie"],
        ("girls", "cartoon"): d["girls_per_cartoon"],
        ("girls", "kids_movie"): d["girls_per_kids_movie"],
    }
    requirement = {
        "boys": d["min_boys"],
        "girls": d["min_girls"],
    }

    # Constraint: each audience group must reach its minimum exposure
    def audience_rule(m, g):
        return sum(exposure[(g, k)] * m.x[k] for k in m.M) >= requirement[g]

    model.audience = pyo.Constraint(model.G, rule=audience_rule)

    return model
